articleTitle: Advances in Materials and Device Technologies
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This session opens with an invited review by J. Murphy of the various types of III-V transistors being developed for use at millimeter-wave frequencies. Contributed papers will then address the increasing availability of 4-in.-diameter GaAs substrates, and the effects of subsurface substrate damage on FET processing. Two papers examining ways of improving the basic GaAs MESFET are followed by a discussion of modeling applied to the representation of device and process technology. Finally, after a paper detailing the characterization of high speed photodetectors for opto-electronic co-integration, the session concludes with an advanced device concept for reduced component-count circuits using resonant tunneling diodes.

articleTitle: Digital Integrated Circuits—I
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Digital GaAs integrated circuits have been maturing rapidly during the last year. Evidence to this is given by the achievements in memory circuits. In the first part of this session, memory circuits will be discussed, including a sub-nanosecond access time 4K RAM, a 16K low standby power static RAM, a complementary JFET 4K RAM, and a 4K ROM.

articleTitle: Evening Panel Discussion: Optical Testing of GaAs ICs
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This session will cover the potential benefits of optical testing, as well as some of the technological limitations which must be resolved to foster broader applications of these techniques.

articleTitle: Advanced Processes and Circuits
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This session focuses on new technologies for digital circuit applications, including Heterojunction Bipolar Transistors (HBTs) and enhancement-mode MESFETs. HBT technology is highlighted in an invited paper by S. Evans, et.al which describes an LSI-oriented heterojunction I<sup>2</sup>L process that is already in pilot production. Additional papers report the use of HBTs in ultra-high speed SSI circuits and in MSI-complexity analog-to-digital and digital-to-analog converters.

articleTitle: Digital Integrated Circuits—II
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This session begins with a paper describing an 8 × 8 matrix switch for use in high speed digital communications at rates of over 1 Gb/s. The next three papers describe several types of multiply and multiply-accumulate circuits; two utilize MESFET technology while the third uses a self-aligned MODFET process. Each multiplier uses a different architectural approach to optimize performance.

articleTitle: Evening Panel Discussion: Production Testing of GaAs MMICs and Millimeter-Wave ICs
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: As the microwave and millimeter-wave applications for GaAs MMICs make the transition from design development to large quantity production, the screening and testing of MMICs must be improved to meet the cost and through-put goals of production. RF and microwave test equipment developers have supported the traditional design market but are now adapting to the requirements of large volume users. New test techniques and philosophies must be developed for the microwave test environment which is concerned with analog signals, in contrast to the more mature digital test applications.

articleTitle: Evening Panel Discussion: GaAs IC AND MMIC RELIABILITY
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This panel session will review the reliability status of GaAs MMICs and digital ICs. The discussion will focus on the issues of reliability and trade-off with yield, performance, and manufacturability. Various experiences on high yield MMICs will be reviewed. Panel members wil give short presentations on the reliability of commercially available parts and then will discuss the issues between yield, manufacturability, and reliability.

articleTitle: High Speed A/D Converter and Signal Processing Techniques
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The development of signal processing integrated circuits is another indication of the growing maturity of GaAs technology. These circuits often perform valuable interface functions between complex digital integrated circuits and the "outside" world. This session begins with an invited paper by H. Kawai and N. Watanabe discussing the prospects of MOCVD technology for GaAs integrated circuit fabrication. This is followed by a variety of papers discussing novel circuits for signal processing applications, including two A/D converters (one in HBT and the other in MESFET technology), a digital-to-analog sine converter, an integrated laser driver and optical receiver, an operational amplifier, a dual bridge sample-and-hold, and a pin driver.

articleTitle: Wideband Amplifiers and Other MMIC Components
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This session presents wideband amplifiers and other MMIC components covering the range 0.05 - 20 GHz. The first paper discusses a 6 -18 GHz low noise amplifier with 4 dB noise figure and 20 dB gain realized on a 3.0 × 2.4 × 0.1 mm chip. In another paper, an LNA utilizing dual feedback circuits has demonstrated 1.8 dB noise figure with 23 dB gain across 0.2 - 2.0 GHz with an MMIC that draws only 21 mA.

articleTitle: System Applications, Electro-Optic Sampling, and IC Reliability
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The first two invited papers of the Symposium review areas that represent two of the most exciting and potentially significant markets for gallium arsenide devices. The first, by D. Kiefer and J. Heightley, describes the digital circuits and packaging that are under development for the CRAY-3, a 16 Giga-Flop Computer. The second, by A. Podell, deals with the design of linear MMICs to operate over wide frequency and temperature ranges with applications to military, space, and communications systems.

articleTitle: High Speed, Low-Power GaAs Programmable Counters for Synthesizer Applications
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: For use in high-speed frequency synthesizer applications, we have developed a number of low-power GaAs DCFL components, including a divide-by-two circuit (5.1 GHz, 1.9 mW), dual-modulus (+10/11) prescaler (2.35 GHz, 15 mW), 4-bit ripple counter (2.35 GHz, 4.6 mW), 4-bit programmable prescaler (1.7 GHz, 36 mW), and a 4-bit programmable counter with ECL-compatible I/0s (1.8 GHz, 70 mW, excluding output drivers). The circuits are fabricated with a high-yield refractory self-aligned gate process, and operate over a wide variation in power supply voltage and temperature. When operated at a package temperature of 125°C, the circuits show less than a 10% degradation in their maximum clock frequency. The results demonstrate state-of-the-art high-frequency performance at extremely low power dissipation.

articleTitle: A Comparison Study of GaAs E/D-MESFETs Fabricated with Self-Aligned and Non-Self-Aligned Processes
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The device characteristics and circuit performance of a self-aligned and a non-self-aligned GaAs E/D-MESFETs have been compared. The fabrication process for the self-aligned MESFETs was similar to the SAINT process [1], with modifications made to enhance yield and to facilitate double-level-metal interconnection. The non-self-aligned MESFETs were fabricated with the conventional recessed-gate process. Electrical measurements across a 2-inch wafer showed that an average self-aligned, 40-µm-wide, 1-μm-long enhancement device has a transconductance of 275 ± 17 mS/mm, a K-value of 16.3 ± 2.7 mS/V, a series resistance of 0.88 ± 0.1 ohm-mm, and a threshold deviation of 28 mV. Corresponding data for the non- self-aligned devices were 191 ± 19 mS/mm, 10.3 ± 1.4 mS/V, 1.2 ± 0.2 ohm-mm, and 45 mV, respectively. A low-power-design ECL-compatible 1-kbit static RAM was fabricated. By using the self-aligned process and a higher depletion threshold, power of the SRAM was reduced from 530 mW for the non-self-aligned SRAM to 220 mW while access times remained the same.

articleTitle: Q-Band Monolithic GaAs Impatt Oscillator
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A fully monolithic GaAs IMPATT oscillator has been fabricated for operation at 44 GHz. In pulsed operation, the oscillator gave 320 mW peak at 5 percent efficiency at the output of the chip, with a 300 nS pulse at 6 percent duty cycle. The circuit elements needed to resonate and bias the diode were realized in microstrip directly on semi-insulating GaAs. Molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) was used to deposit the active layers of the double-drift Read IMPATT diode as well as a GaAlAs layer. The GaAlAs served as an etch barrier layer in the via-hole fabrication process. In this paper, we describe our approach to device design, fabrication, and testing.

articleTitle: Investigation on Interelectrode Metallic "Paths" Affecting the Operation of IC MESFETs
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: An evaluation has been made on GaAs digital IC components (on both DCFL and BFL electrical configurations). A major failure mode affected the depletion-mode FETs. It was due to the development of intereiectrode metallic paths during processing or aging. Analysis have been conducted by means of Scanning Optical Microscopy, high resolution Auger Spectroscopy and Secondary Ion Mass Spectrome try. Two formation mechanisms are involved: (i) gradual release of elemental metallic As during processing and, (ii) electric-field induced Au migration (from the ohmic contacts) in the presence of As oxide, during aging.

articleTitle: A Monolithic Integrated 35 GHZ Receiver Employing a Schottky Diode Mixer and a Mesfet IF Amplifier
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A GaAs monolithic 35 GHz receiver consisting of a single balanced microstrip mixer and a single stage IF amplifier has been developed. The receiver was fabricated using a planar technology incorporating a buried layer to reduce the series resistance of the Schottky mixer diodes. An unusual technology employing a deep selective n<sup>+</sup> implantation for the buried n<sup>+</sup> zones and MOCVD epitaxial overgrowth of the implanted substrate to form the η layer has been developed for the fabrication of this circuit. The single balanced mixer achieved a conversion loss of 7.2 dB and a double side band noise figure of 6.5 dB at 35 GHz. The single stage feedback amplifier achieved a gain of > 10 dB over the 0.5 - 1.5 GHz IF band.

articleTitle: Transient Radiation Upset of GaAs Buffered FET Logic ICs
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Transient radiation effects were studied in a number of GaAs buffered FET logic (BFL) ICs including ripple counters, NOR gates, and ring oscillators. The hardness level was found to depend more on the dose per pulse than on dose rate; the apparent hardness level increases with increasing dose rate. Depending on the circuit, upset resulted from changes in circuit bias resulting from large FET photocurrents, induced oscillations during the photocurrent, and long term FET currents resulting from charge trapped in the substrate. Electron and hole trapping levels were determined by measuring the temperature dependence of the long term current transients.

articleTitle: 100 mm GaAs Substrates for Mimic Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: In order to assess the quality of available 100 mm GaAs substrates, arrays of test transistors were processed on four wafers supplied by three different vendors. Both dc and RF device parameters of the transistors were measured, and the results compared to values typically obtained on 3-inch start ing material. The best device results from the 100 mm starting material were comparable to typical values for devices fabricated on 3-inch material; however, the mean values of transconductance (gm), saturation current (Id<inf>ss</inf>) and maximum available RF gain at 10 GHz were lower. The standard deviations for all of these parameters was also larger for FETs fabricated on 100 mm material. Our results indicated that 100 mm GaAs substrates are promi sing candidates for GaAs pilot line production.

articleTitle: High Performance Monolithic Power Amplifier using All RIE Etch Process
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A high performance X-band monolithic power amplifier has been fabricated using high-yield, planar ion implanted, and all reactive ion etching (RIE) processes. Device characteristics are improved by a unique gate etch profile of RIE/WET combined recess process. The two-stage power amplifier has achieved the performance of 2.5 watts maximum output power (power density: 0.69 W/mm) with 9.4 dB associated gain and 30 percent of best power-added efficiency at 9.5 GHz. The overall dc yield of the amplifier is improved from 20 to 30 percent with this all-RIE dry etch process.

articleTitle: A Self-Aligned Planar GaAs Mesfet Technology for MMICs
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A self-aligned gate MESFET technology for high performance and high yield MMICs is described. To reduce the gate resistance, a Ti/Au layer is added onto a WSix refractory gate. An LDD (Lightly Doped Drain) structure is also adopted to increase the gate breakdown voltage and reduce the gate capacitance. Standard deviation of Idss is about 6% over a 2"Φ wafer. In a 0.5µm gate FET, cut-off frequency (fT) of 42GHz and noise figure (NFmin) at 12GHz of 1.25dB are obtained. NFmin less than 1.4dB is obtained with an excellent yield higher than 80%.

articleTitle: On the Applications of Laser-Direct-Writing Techniques to GaAs Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Laser-direct-write deposition of tungsten has been developed as a convenient and versatile technique for postfabrication trimming of GaAs monolithic microwave integrated circuits. Tungsten microstrip lines of 30 μΩ-cm resistivity are deposited via a vapor-phase reaction induced by a focused argon-ion laser beam with micrometer position accuracy. The deposited W lines can also be easily removed by laser ablation. These W microstrip lines have been successfully used for tuning an 8-GHz GaAs MESFET amplifier and a 30-GHz monolithic attenuator.

articleTitle: A Manufacturable Low-Power 16K-BIT GaAs Sram
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A manufacturable 16K-bit GaAs static RAM has been designed and fabricated using LSI depletion mode MESFET technology. Large dc margins and low standby power consumption were the primary goals of the circuit design. To date, the highest bit yield chips produced have only one repeating bad bit.

articleTitle: Process and Devices Models for GaAs Mesfet Technology
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Two process models for GaAs MESFET technology are described: SUPREM 3.5 and GEM. The models share new data on the implantation of Si, Se, and Be ions into GaAs and their diffusion during annealing. While SUPREM is a process model code designed for integration with Stanford University's general device-modeling codes, GEM is a MESFET-application-specific code. A comparison of GEM's predictions with measured MESFET electrical characteristics is made. The code is used to assess possible methods for fabricating higher-perfomance enhancement-mode MESFETs.

articleTitle: A 1.2 NS GaAs 4kb Read-Only-Memory Fabricated by 0.5 µm-Gate BP-Saint
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A fully functional 4kb GaAs Read Only Memory has been demonstrated with an access time of 1.2 ns and a power dissipation of 3.75 W including ECL-compatibie I/O buffers. In the design, a new single-transistor-type memory cell and an E/D DCFL for peripheral circuits are adopted. In the fabrication, a 0.5 µm-gate BP-SAINT is used where typical E-FETs have a transconductance of 260 mS/mm.

articleTitle: Integration of GaAs/AlAs Resonant Tunneling Diodes for Digital and Analog Applications with Reduced Circuit Complexity
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A new approach to obtain multiple peaks in the current-voltage characteristic by integrating Resonant Tunneling (RT) diodes is demonstrated. The peaks are generated using only the ground state resonance of the quantum well rather than several states, as in conventional RT devices. The separation between the peaks is voltage tunable and also the peak currents can be made nearly equal, which is necessary to use the device in a variety of circuit applications. A functional IC operating at 100K, with two peaks in the I-V has been fabricated. The first practical demonstration of circuits for a 3-state memory, frequency multiplication by a factor of 5 and 4-bit parity generation, using a single functional RT structure each is also reported. The use of multiple-peak RT devices in these circuits results in considerable reduction in the number of component per function over conventional techniques.

articleTitle: Evening Panel Discussion: GaAs-on-Si: Ready for GaAs ICs?
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: When will GaAs-on-Si be ready for IC fabrication? (Or, when will it be all that it's cracked up to be?) Will GaAs-on-Si emerge unscathed by the problems of stress and defects? Or will it buckle under to the intense pressure for providing a large, robust, cheap surrogate substrate for GaAs ICs? As for applications, what is real: large, durable, cheap wafers for digital and MMIC circuits or co-integration of GaAs and Si ICs? What about optical interconnects and optical integrated circuits? In summary, is GaAs-on-Si real for IC or is it the proverbial house built on sand, eventually to disappear into the oblivion of so many good ideas?

articleTitle: A GaAs Bit-Slice Microprocessor Chip Set
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A GaAs chip set comprising the critical path elements for a bit-slice microprocessor family is described. The 3-chip set consists of a 4-bit slice multifunction ALU with an on-board 16 × 42-port RAM, a 12-bit programmable sequencer and a carry look-ahead generator for a 16-bit wide data path. These devices, which are currently in production, are architecturally and functionally equivalent to the Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) 2901, 2910A, and 2902, respectively. These chips were developed utilizing the Vitesse Semiconductor Corp. Vl process, which is a GaAs MESFET self-aligned gate enhancement depletion (E/D) process, designed to optimize reproducibility of digital LSI. Performance of a 16-bit microprocessor system implemented in this technology is compared with the traditional bit-slice approach using silicon parts, and is shown to be at least a factor of 3 faster.

articleTitle: A 6-18 GHz Monolithic Low Noise Amplifier
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A 6- to 18-GHz monolithic low-noise amplifier with high gain was designed and fabricated. The device was produced using production-adaptable MMIC techniques. 22 dB gain with 4.5 dB noise figure was achieved from 7.5 to 17.5 GHz. The current to gain efficiency was approximately 4.1 mA/dB.

articleTitle: MOCVD Technology for Compound Semiconductor Devices
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The present state of MOCVD (metal organic chemical vapor deposition) technology is reviewed as a means for producing high-speed devices based on AlGaAs/GaAs heterointerfaces. Atomically abrupt heterointerfaces and tailored gradient interfaces can be grown with precise control. Doping profiles produced by MOCVD are also satisfactory for most purposes. A growth system with a capacity of seven 2-inch-wafers/run was developed to test Its feasibility for mass-producing heterointerface devices. Uniformity of growth parameters both within wafers and among wafers is satisfactory. N-channel HIFETs (HEMT) were grown by this system. The average noise figure of 0.5 um-gate length HIFETs at 12 GHz was 0.96 dB with a standard déviation of 0.06 dB on a 2-inch wafer. The standard déviation of a pinch-off voltage of 100um × 100 um-FAT-HIFET was 9.7 mV, with an average voltage of -509 mV among 246 samples in a 16 mm × 16 mm area. Compositional grading and selective area epitaxy are shown to be important advantages of MOCVD which improves device performance.

articleTitle: A 5 Gb/s GaAs Monolithic Master-Slave D-Type Flip Flop IC
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A high-speed, high-sensitivity GaAs master-slave D-type Flip Flop IC has been developed for realizing very high-speed communication systems and test instruments. A maximum operating speed of 5 Gb/s and an input signal sensitivity of 400 mV at 5 Gb/s were obtained using 0.8 um long WSi gate self-alignment FET technology and improved ECL compatible circuit design approach including input and output circuits for high speed operation.

articleTitle: A 1-20 GHz Dual Gate Distributed Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The design, modeling, fabrication and performance of a broadband distributed amplifier, employing power dual-gate FETs, will be described. This highly producible amplifier is capable of operating throughout the entire 1 to 20 GHz frequency range exhibiting an average gain of 8.6 dB and a power output of 0.5 Watt. A nonlinear analysis, which can predict the power limitations and power output performance of distributed structures will also be included in this discussion.

articleTitle: A 4-Bit Quantizer Implemented with AlGaAs/GaAs Heterojunction Bipolar Transistors
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This paper reports a 4-bit quantizer implemented with AlGaAs/GaAs Heterojunction Bipolar Transistors for use in high-speed analog to digital conversion. The circuit contains 16 voltage comparators, a resistor ladder for reference voltage generation, encoding logic, and output buffers. Proper operation of quantizers at sampling rates higher than 1 Gsps was demonstrated. The static non-linearity was consistent with 8-bit accuracy.

articleTitle: A High CMRR GaAs Operational Amplifier IC
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: We demonstrate a GaAs operational amplifier having such a high common-mode rejection ratio (CMRR) as 63 dB with a unity-gain frequency of 150 MHz. This dramatic improvement has been achieved by adopting the common-mode feedback and cascaded differential amplifiers with the dual-gate FET configuration.

articleTitle: Push-Push, Frequency-Doubling, MMIC Oscillators
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Push-push, frequency-doubling, dielectric resonator oscillators have been demonstrated using existing C-band and K<inf>u</inf>-band push-pull MMIC chips. The demonstrations show the practicality of using MMIC designs where gain balance and phase tracking are critical. Optimized MMIC push-push DROs are expected to show excellent performance through K<inf>a</inf>-band. The 5.8 GHz push-push DRO showed: -50 dBc fundamental suppression; 0.2% stability over -54°C to +85°C; -100 dBc/Hz phase noise at 100 KHz; and low power consumption, 50 mA at +12 VDC for 10 dBm output power.

articleTitle: A 100ps GaAs Pin Driver Suitable for High-Speed Test Systems
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A 100ps pin driver with adjustable output levels will be described. The differential outputs can deliver more than 2 volts each into 50 ohm loads within a window of greater than +/- 2.5 volts. The outputs are reverse terminated into 50 ohms and can be forced through these resistors to a termination voltage such as -2 volts. The inputs are ECL compatible and can be driven differentially or single ended. An on chip ECL reference voltage is provided. The circuit can also switch between 0.5 and 4.5 volts when driving a TTL or CMOS load. The maximum data rate is greater than 3 GHz NRZ.

articleTitle: An L-Band Variable-Gain Amplifier GaAs MMIC with Precise Binary Step Control
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This paper describes the design and performance of an L-band GaAs variable-gain amplifier MMIC. The amplifier's output amplitude can be adjusted over a 50 dB range with 6 bits of precision and with minimum insertion phase variation from state to state. The measured maximum RMS amplitude error is less than 2% and the peak insertion phase error is less than 2° for all 64 states.

articleTitle: A 3.0 ns, 330 mW 8 × 8 GaAs Booth's Multiplier
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A 8 × 8 parallel multiplier, operating in 2's complement mode, is described. Tne circuit, implementing the modified Booth's algorithm, uses both E/R DCFL and transfer logic cells. The best multiplication time measured on fabricated chips is 3 ns, which corresponds to 115 ps average gate delay. The associated power consumption is 330 mW.

articleTitle: A Novel Fully Self-Aligned Closely-Spaced-Electrode HBT for SSI Logic Family Applications
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This paper deals with the design consideration, fabrication process, and performances of small-scale integrated (SSI) logic circuits implemented using newly developed self-aligned AlGaAs/GaAs heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs). The logic circuits include an INVERTER, OR/NOR, NAND/OR, EXCLUSIVE OR/NOR, and FLIP-FLOPs constructed using current-mode logic (CML) gates. Each IC consumes about 30 mW of dc power for a successful operation with a chip yield higher than 50%. Preliminary experimental results with input frequencies higher than 1-GHz indicate capability of these circuits for "GHz" class operation. SPICE-F simulation show potential for proper operation with clock/input frequencies exceeding 4 GHz.

articleTitle: 8×8-Bit Pipelined Parallel Multiplier Utilizing Self-Aligned Gate n+ -(Al,Ga)As/GaAs MODFET IC Technology
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: An 8×8-bit pipelined parallel multiplier utilizing self-aligned gate n<sup>+</sup>-(Al,Ga)As/GaAs modulation-doped FETs (MODFETs) has been demonstrated. The fully functional multipliers operated to clock frequencies (gate delays) of 510 MHz (70 ps/gate) at corresponding chip power dissipations (gate power dissipations) of 1.9 W (1.4 mW/gate) at room temperature. This corresponds to an intrinsic multiply time of 3.2 ns. This is the shortest gate delay ever reported for an LSI complexity circuit using any semiconductor IC technology at room temperature.

articleTitle: A Submicron Self-Aligned Gate GaAs Mesfet Technology for Low Power Subnanosecond Static RAM Fabrication
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A high performance submicron gate GaAs MESFET process has been successfully developed using the self-aligned gate approach. Tungsten Nitride (WN<inf>X</inf>) refractory metal has been used as the gate metal for higher gate turn-on voltage. A p-buried layer was implanted under the channel using Be<sup>+</sup> to reduce short-channel effects as well as to improve FET uniformity. Transconductance as high as 300 mS/mm was achieved for a 0.6 µm gate with threshold voltage uniformity of one standard deviation as low as 16.8 mV across a 3-inch undoped LEC wafer and 7.6 mV for a 13×13 FET array. Using this process we have fabricated 256×4 bit SRAM with access time of 1 ns with a power consumption of only 300 mW.

articleTitle: CRAY-3: A Gaas Implemented Supercomputer System
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The CRAY-3 computer, currently in development, has a performance goal of > 10 Giga-Flops. For ultra-high speed at modest power levels, GaAs IC logia was selected. Performance levels of < 150 ps/gate are achieved using a custom GaAs IC logic cell approach comprised of 40-80 multi-level logic cells equivalent to 200-300 GaAs logic gates. An efficient fast turn design methodology has been developed to effectively generate the 200 logic designs used in the computer. GaAs ICs based on a low voltage D-MESFET technology are fabricated (on a foundry basis) at GigaBit Logic. Average circuit yields of >45% have been achieved with peak yields in the 75-80% range. Unique high density packaging techniques (developed in-house at Cray Research) are used to preserve the high performance of GaAs ICs at the system level. This system contains ~ 48,000 logic chips and ~40,000 memory chips and will be the first major electronic system to be implemented with GaAs logic.

articleTitle: A Gb/s 16:1 Multiplexer and 1:16 Demultiplexer Chip Set with High Yield and Low Power Dissipation
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A Gb/s 16:1 multiplexer (MUX) and 1:16 demultiplexer (DMUX) chip set with ECL and TTL I/O interfaces has been designed and fabricated. The circuit was mainly constructed by DCFL to realize below 1W power dissipation in a chip with 300-400 gates, while push/pull circuits were used in case of heavy loading conditi ons. Chips were fabricated by a 1. 2μια refractory WN<inf>X</inf> gate LDD structure FET process. Chip yields were as high as 7196 and 55% for the MUX and the DMUX, respectively. The chips operated up to 1.4GHz and 1.0GHz clock frequency with 0.64W and 0.86W power dissipation for the MUX and the DMUX, respectively.

articleTitle: Gallium Arsenide MESFET Technologies with 0.7 µm Gate-Length for 4kb 1ns Static RAM
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Gallium Arsenide MESFET technologies with 0.7µm gate-length are developed for 4kb Ins Static RAM. For the practical use of GaAs SRAM, the high-speed performance is naturally very important. And another important item is the reliability, for example, the immunity of soft-errors induced by alpha-particles. In this study, the additional p-type layer is newly introduced in the GaAs MESFET for both the suppression of short-channel effect and the improvement of soft-error immunity. This technology was successfully applied to a 4kb SRAM. The access time of 1 ns was obtained in the 4kb SRAM.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Monolithic Integrated Circuits and MMIC Probing Techniques
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: GaAs millimeter and microwave monolithic integrated circuits (MIMICs) have promised high potential for reducing microwave system cost. A host of innovative and more complex GaAs MIMICs and processes is leveraging the technology into a new era. In this session, a number of applications, and the technologies that produce them will be discussed. Two papers describe 30 and 35 GHz monolithic receivers fabricated using Schottky diode and MESFET technologies for satellite feed array and receiver applications. In another, the reactive ion etch technique is used to fabricate a high performance MIMIC. A monolithic oscillator is demonstrated at 44 GHz. State of the art performance has been achieved by a monolithic GaAs PIN diode at 65 GHz, and a buried channel MESFET structure has shown improved performance over conventional MESFETs. The use of laser direct write techniques for the fabrication of GaAs MIMICs is the topic of one of the process presentations. In the final paper of the session, a GaAs MIMIC gain block fabricated on a GaAs/Si substrate is discussed.

articleTitle: GaAs Integrated Circuit Measurements using Electrooptic Sampling
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The principles of electrooptic sampling for IC testing, its capabilities as both a time-domain sampling oscilloscope and a frequency-domain network analyzer, and recent measurements results are described. Applications of this system include measurements of internal-node switching signals and propagation delays in digital circuits with picosecond time resolution, smallsignal and large-signal analysis of microwave circuits, and measurement of the one-port S-parameters on IC transmission lines to millimeter-wave frequencies. A method to measure two-port S-parameters using the optical probe is described. This technique defines an on-chip reference plane, reducing measurement errors and eliminating the calibration standards and routines required with conventional network analyzers.

articleTitle: A 1GHz-2mA/5V GaAs 128/129 Prescaler IC
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A low-power dissipation 128/129 dual modulus prescaler IC was developed using a lightly doped drain self-aligned WSi gate (LDD SAG) FET process. This process gives both a high transconductance (gm) and a high gate-to-source breakdown voltage (Vgso), resulting in low-power dissipation and high reliability. Low power of 1.8mA/5V was achieved at the maximum operating frequency of 1.1GHz. In addition, for practical use, this IC mounted in a plastic mold package was tested for reliability and no degradation was observed.

articleTitle: Monolithic Transmit/Receive Switch for Millimeter-Wave Application
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A state-of-the-art RF performance has been achieved for a monolithic millimeter-wave GaAs PIN diode switch. The planar microstrip PIN diode switch is fabricated on a 4-mil thick semi-insulating GaAs substrate utilizing advanced selective ion implantation technique. The measured insertion loss for the switch-on path is less than 1.5 dB across a 6 GHz bandwidth (59-65 GHz) for two shunt-mounted PIN diodes· The isolation, switchoff, is also measured to be greater than -30 dB across 4 GHz bandwidth (62.5-66.5 GHz). The monolithic PIN diode switch circuit has also demonstrated a switching speed of less than 2A nanoseconds and RF power handling capability in excess of 1.6 Watts.

articleTitle: Reliability Evaluation of a GaAs IC Pre-Amplifier HIC
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This work evaluates the reliability of a GaAs IC chip mounted on a Hybrid Integrated Circuit (HIC). The HIC serves as a transimpedance pre-amplifier in lightwave transmission applications. The GaAs IC chip is fabricated using etched gate, depletion mode, n-channel FETs with Ti/Pt/Au gate and interconnect metallization. A silicon resin is applied to the GaAs chip for protection. The high temperature operational bias aging has been carried out at three temperatures. The failure distributions have a sigma (lognormal) of 1.1 and show an activation energy of 1.1 eV. The predicted failure rate is less than 100 FITs for an operation ambient of 75 °C. The temperature-humidity-bias aging (85/85/bias) showed no failures in 1×10<sup>5</sup> device hours. These results predict a failure rate of 20 FITs at 50 C and 55% R.H.

articleTitle: III-V Transistors for MM-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The ability to operate at frequencies at and above 60 GHz is desirable in many applications to increase bandwidth, achieve more favorable tradeoffs between antenna beamwidth and size, and to exploit frequency dependent transmission properties of the atmosphere. Table 1 provides a listing of important requirements for EHF radar, communications and electronic warfare systems. Corresponding device and circuit requirements are delineated. One especially demanding requirement is to develop phased arrays at 60 and 94 GHz. At 94 GHz this requires an array of transmit/receive (T/R) modules with center to center spacings of 1.5 mm between modules. Generating the required output power without exceeding thermal dissipation limits places stringent requirements on the solid state components of the T/R module.

articleTitle: Characteristics of 30 GHz MMIC Receivers for Satellite Feed Array Application
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: RF characteristics of a 30 GHz "front-end" receiver incorporating three monolithic chips are presented. The ion-implanted GaAs MMIC chips include a 7 dB noise figure, 10 dB gain front-end amplifier, a 5-bit phase shifter and a 12 dB gain control amplifier. All three functions are accomplished at the receive frequency (27.5 - 30 GHz). Data presented for the interconnected receiver includes gain/loss measurements, relative phase shift measurements and noise figure. Characteristics from three such recieve modules are summarized and discussed.

articleTitle: Depletion Mode GaAs IC Reliability
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This work presents results of MSI GaAs reliability testing. Previously reported methods of element-based IC reliability prediction are verified and additional element results are briefly described. This report is the culmination of reliability testing on over 2700 circuit elements and 100 ICs. Each of the failures have been classified and failure rate distributions have been established where appropriate. Element studies confirmed gate metal diffusion is the primary failure mechanism. These findings are used in the determination of IC failure distributions. Two accelerated lifetests, totaling over 100,000 (non-derated) device-hours, have been completed on MSI (30 gate equivalency) four-bit ripple counters. An additional lifetest has been completed on a larger scale (300 gate equivalency) ASIC digital circuit. A comparison of IC and element median lives reveals a nonlinear relationship between integration level and reliability. For example, the single FET median life at 150°C was found to be only 3 times longer than the median life of the 300 gate equivalency (1000 MESFET) device. Thus, IC failure rates are less than whole multiples of FET failure rates. IC lifetests have also indicated that reliability levels vs fabrication date are rapidly improving for GaAs ICs. 30 Gate devices tested in the most recent lifetest have 150°C median lives ten times longer (6.5E5 vs 6.0E4 hrs) than ICs manufactured six months earlier. Preliminary data on microwave ICs indicate similar results.

articleTitle: Subsurface Damage in Semi-Insulating GaAs Substrates
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Studies of subsurface damage in polished three-inch diameter semi-insulating gallium arsenide using photon backscattering, cross-section transmission electron microscopy, and delineation etching gechniques hage found greater polishing damage (10<sup>8</sup> defects cm<sup>-2</sup> ) in undoped than in In-doped wafers which were essentially defect free. Observations of the behavior of thermally activated ion-implanted silicon in polished semi-insulating GaAs substrates, using FET and Hall metrology, indicate that self-compensation of the silicon dopant occurs within the subsurface damage region which is responsible for loss of FET channel current. It is suggested that wafer surface stoichiometry, whether modified by boule annealing, subsurface damage, etching or capping processes, is a first order effect controlling the activation of implanted silicon and consequently the performance and yield of gallium arsenide FETs and ICs.

articleTitle: Buried-Channel GaAs MESFETs with Improved Small-Signal Characteristics
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Buried-channel GaAs MESFETs with quarter micron gate lengths have been fabricated by ion implantation into undoped LEC material. Compared to conventional half and one micron MESFETs, these devices exhibit higher gain, wider bandwidth, reduced short channel effects, and much less dispersion and frequency dependence of the small-signal parameter values. These improvements are obtained because the carrier trapping at the channel-substrate and channel-surface interfaces, common in a conventional MESFET, is considerably reduced in the buried-channel MESFET by the presence of the implanted p-type layers. Improved small-signal device characteristics will likely expand the range of applications for GaAs MESFET technology into precision analog and mixed analog-digital subsystems not currently exploited by GaAs.

articleTitle: A High Speed 1K × 4-Bit Static RAM using 0.5 µm-Gate HEMT
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: An ECL-compatible IK × 4-bit static RAM has been developed using 0.5-μm gate HEMT technology. The short channel effect of HEMT is much smaller than that of GaAs MESFET. Submicron HEMT technology is a promising candidate for high-speed LSI applications. Using an accurate HEMT model developed for circuit simulation of submicron HEMT LSIs, the RAM circuit was optimized to achieve high-speed performance and ECL-compatibi 1 i ty at room temperature. The data line equalization technique was adopted in the RAM cicuit design to reduce address access time. An X-address access time of 0.5 ns was measured at room temperature for a chip power dissipation of 5.7 W. The minimum write-enable pulsewidth was less than 1 ns.

articleTitle: Low-Noise GaAs MESFET by Dummy-Gate Self-Alignment Technology for MMIC
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A low noise microwave GaAs MESFET has been developed by using a dummy-gate self-alignment process. The newly developed process with submicron gate length of 0.3 µm, shallow ion implantation in the active channel, source-drain fabrication by N+ ion implantation self-aligned with dummy-gate, and low gate resistance by adopting T-shaped gate, is employed for low noise chracteristics. Noise figure as 1.1 dB and associated gain as 9.5 dB are obtained in the dummy gate self-alined FET with 140 µm gatewidth.

articleTitle: X-Band MMIC Amplifier on GaAs/Si
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A single-stage MMIC feedback amplifier fabricated on GaAs epitaxially grown on high-resistivity Si (6×10 ohm-cm) will be described. The amplifier had 5.5 dB maximum small signal gain and a 3-dB bandwidth of 8.5 to 11.5 GHz. The performance was limited by the poor quality of the Schottky ba rrier on GaAs/Si. The thermal resistance of the MESFET in this MMIC was measured and found to be considerably lower than that for a comparable unit on a semi-insulating GaAs substrate.

articleTitle: A 4K × 1 Bit Complementary E-JFET Static RAM
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A 4K × 1 bit static RAM, based on a six transistor complementary memory cell, has been designed fabricated and tested. The circuit uses enhancement mode n- and p-channel JFET transistors and p- and n-type resistors. SRAMs in packages were tested to be fully functional with the GALPAT test pattern. Chip size was 3.9 mm × 4.9 mm. Typical power dissipation was 200 mW and typical access time was 10 ns.

articleTitle: On-Chip Characterization of Fully Integrated Photoreceivers using High-Yield Ion-Implanted GaAs IC Technology
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Metal-semiconductor-metal photodetectors (MSM) has been fabricated on ion-implanted GaAs IC substrate as the front end detector for a wideband integrated transimpedance amplifier. The performance of MSM detectors with standard 1 um Ti/Pt/Au gate metalization and -1 V pinch-off voltage on n-channel, semi-insulating substrate and n+ implantation are compared. No extra mask or processing steps is required. The MSM detector on n- channel gate implant has the best optimized performance. It has high break-down voltage, low dark current and high-speed linear response under illumination. A 3-dB bandwidth of 1.5 GHz and 15 dB gain has been observed for the resultant receiver front end amplifier.

articleTitle: A 7K GaAs Configurable Cluster Gate Array
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A large scale, low power 7056 gate configurable cluster array has been designed, fabricated and tested. The array employed 1 µm gate length MESFETs on 3-in. GaAs wafers using a planar fabrication process. A unique configurable logic cluster utilizing buffered FET logic (BFL) that is internally routable was designed. Internal routability of the cluster allows for the configuration of up to eight-gate high level logic functions, including edge-triggered flip flops, without the use of external routing channels. The use of a cluster design methodology reduces parasitic loading effects due to interconnects necessary to generate many logic functions, thereby increasing the speed of a personalized system. The logic gate design employs the use of narrow, 3 µm, -0.5 V threshold devices. The pullup and pulldown devices have been sized equally to obtain large dc noise margins and decreased temperature sensitivity for operation over the military temperature range of -55°C to 125°C. The design of the basic BFL gate and the cluster allows for the use of a new complex gating technique whereby input transistors can supply either inverting or noninverting inputs. Several complex gates have been developed as part of the macrocell library for use in this array. Included are a one gate delay exclusive OR (EXOR) gate which dissipates less power than conventional exclusive or gate designs, and an edge-triggered D flip-flop with a clock to data delay of four-gate delays rather than the five-gate delays of traditional designs.

articleTitle: 26-GHz GaAs Room-Temperature Dynamic Divider Circuit
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This paper describes the operation of a buffered FET logic (BFL) dynamic divider fabricated with advanced processes such as 0.2-μm gate length MESFETs, active channels grown with molecular beam epitaxy (MBE), and airbridge interconnects. The divider operated up to 26.5 GHz at room temperature at a power dissipation of 310 mW. Electro-optic techniques were used to verify divider operation.

articleTitle: Wideband C/X/KU Power MMICS
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Four wideband power MMIC's covering suboctave and multi-octave bands within 4.5 to 18 GHz and power levels of 0.4 to 3.0 Watts are described. The two-stage 6.5 to 16.5 GHz chip has produced 0.4 to 0.8 watts with a power-added efficiency of 25 to 33 % across 7.5 to 11.5 GHz, and as a linear power amplifier has produced 300mW with less than -18 dBc intermodulation distortion at 12 Ghz. The two-stage 7 to 11 Ghz MMIC has produced 1 Watt minimum and 1.5 Watts across a 25 % band with power-added efficiencies of 21 to 29 %. The three-stage 7 to 11 GHz MMIC produces 3 Watts from 7.5 to 10 Ghz and is believed to be the highest reported power level across this bandwidth for an MMIC at X-band. The three-stage 4.5 to 18 GHz 1 Watt minimum chip is the widest bandwidth lossy/reactively matched power MMIC reported at this power level.

articleTitle: A 4-Bit Single Chip Analog to Digital Converter with a 1.0 Gigahertz Analog Input Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A 4-bit ADC (Analog-to-Digital Converter) has been designed and fabricated on a single Gallium Arsenide chip. This device is believed to be the first single chip implementation of a complete GaAs (Gallium Arsenide) ADC, including S/H (sample-and-hold amplifier), quantizer, clock buffer, and output drivers, reported at this level of performance. The circuit was fabricated with an enhancement-depletion self-aligned gate MESFET (E-D SAGFET) process that in­cludes two layers of metallization and laser trimmable thin-film resistors. Preliminary test results using special high frequency wafer probing techniques have demonstrated a full power analog input bandwidth of 1.0 GHz, and correct operation at low input frequency at a 2.5 GHz sample rate without any laser trimming. Recent acquisition of enhanced high speed logic analyzer equipment is expected to allow high speed SNR testing at multigigahertz sampling rates and high input frequencies.

articleTitle: A UHF GaAs Multi-Stage Wideband Amplifier with Dual Feedback Circuits
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A UHF GaAs four-stage wideband amplifier is demonstrated. The amplifier circuit has two feedback loops which are inserted between the output of the 3rd stage and the input of the 1st stage and between the output and the input of the 1st stage. The former allows the wide bandwidth capability, while the latter contributes to lowering the input VSWR. The amplifier was fabricated by using the conventional full ion-implantation process. It exhibited a very flat gain of 23.0 ± 0.5 dB with low input/output VSWRs of less than 2.5 over the frequency range from 0.2 GHz to 2.0 GHz.

articleTitle: A Precision Dual Bridge GaAs Sample and Hold
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A low distortion monolithic GaAs MESFET sample and hold (S/H) has been developed to drive capacitive loads such as large parallel banks of silicon comparators. The S/H is an open loop, single ended design utilizing two Schottky diode sampling bridges in a novel signal bootstrap architecture. The chip is designed to operate over a frequency range from dc to approximately 0.5 GHz, with useful operation extending toward 1 GHz with lighter loads. Initial test results show near ideal performance in a 6-bit 330 Msps analog-to-digital (A/D) system.

articleTitle: Laser Driver and Receiver Amplifiers for 2.4 Gb/s Optical Transmission using WSi-Gate GaAs Mesfet's
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A laser driver IC and receiver amplifier IC's for multi-gigabit optical digital transmission have been designed, fabricated and tested. WSi-gate self-aligned GaAs MESFET's with gate length range of 0.7 to 1.0 μm are implemented in the integrated circuits. It is demonstrated that the operating speed of laser driver IC is as high as 4 Gb/s with NRZ format and that both the bandwidths of preamplifier IC and gain-controllable amplifier IC are 2.4 GHz. These performances meet the fundamental requirements for 2.4 Gb/s optical transmission.

articleTitle: A 0.05- to 14-GHz MMIC 5-Bit Digital Attenuator
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The design approach and the performance of a broadband (0.05- to 14-GHz) digitally controlled MMIC 5-bit attenuator are presented. Attenuator chips with total dimensions of 1.3 × 2.6 mm provide 15.5-dB dynamic range with 0.5-dB step resolution and excellent phase tracking. The circuit consists of a 2-bit chip containing 14 FETs with a total gate periphery of 3.98 mm within an area of 1.3 × 1.2 mm and a 3-bit chip containing 20 FETs with a gate periphery of 5.44 mm within an area of 1.3 × 1.4 mm.

articleTitle: A GaAs Digital-to-Analog Sine Converter
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: We have designed and built a Digital-to-Analog Sine Converter (DASCl using depletion mode technology. The DASC accepts a binary input word and generates complementary current-mode analog outputs, analogously to a linear DAC. However, the output of the DASC is non-linear; an increasing binary count (digital sawtooth) fed to the DASC produces a sinusoidal output. We make explicit use of the symmetry of the cosine function to reduce the size and complexity of the circuit. Random errors are greatly reduced via a guaranteed-monotonic architecture. This circuit was developed to increase the speed and decrease the complexity of Direct Digital Synthesizers. The DASC output waveform exhibits a "spur" level of -34 dBc (measured accuracy is about 1% rms) and consumes 1.5 W of power at a speed of 1.4 Gsample/sec.

articleTitle: GaAs HBT LSI/VLSI Fabrication Technology
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Bipolar HIZL technology has been developed for fabrication of LSI/VLSI circuits with high yields. Using MOCVD epi deposition technique, defects levels of <25/cm<sup>2</sup> have been achieved with gains of 30 to 50 for the emitter-down transistor. In-circuit gates delay of 350 pS for fan-out-of-four has been demonstrated for 2 micron technology and 150 ps predicted for 1.5 micron technology. IK and 4K gate arrays have been fabricated with lot yields of 37% and 10%, respectively. Reliability testing shows ESD tolerance > 2000 volts, full temperature operation and high radiation hardness including SEU.

articleTitle: A 2-W Multistage K-Band GaAs Monolithic Fet Amplifier
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The design, fabrication, and measured performance of K-band MMIC power amplifier modules are described. A single-ended module has demonstrated 27-percent power-added efficiency, better than 513 mW of output power, and 5.2-dB linear gain from 19 to 20.5 GHz. A multistage amplifier exhibited 33-dB linear gain and 2-W output power at 20 GHz. These MMICs include DC-blocking and bias networks.

articleTitle: GaAs Low-Power Parallel Multipliers for a High-Speed Digital Signal Processor
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A 4 × 4-bit and 8 × 8-bit high-speed multiplier have been implemented in low-power GaAs DCFL. Both circuits are fabricated with a high-yield titanium tungsten nitride self-aligned gate MESFET process. The multiplication time for the 4 × 4-bit array multiplier is 940 ps, which is the fastest multiplication time reported for any semiconductor technology. The 8 × 8-bit two's complement multiplier/accumulator uses 4278 FETs (1317 logic gates) and exhibits a multiplication time of 3.17 ns, the fastest yet reported for a multiplier of this type. Yield for the 4 × 4-bit and 8 × 8-bit circuits is 94% and 26% respectively.

articleTitle: Suppression of Sidegating Effect for High Performance GaAs ICs
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Temperature dependence of the sidegatlng effect of GaAs MESFETs was investigated. It was confirmed that the sidegating effect was dominated by two factors; the probability of electrons to reach the depletion region beneath channel, and the capture and emittion rate of deep levels in that region. At low temperature, anomalous sidegating effect was observed, which was not simply eliminated by increasing the distance between an FET and a sidegate. Insertion of negatively biased p-type region formed between them was found to be very effective to suppress the sidegating effect, even at low temperature.

articleTitle: A GaAs 8×8 Matrix Switch LSI for High-Speed Digital Communications
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A GaAs 8×8 matrix switch LSI for high-speed digital communications services, suoh as high-definition (HD) TV, has been fabricated. The switch LSI with fully ECL-compatible interface and -5.2/-2.0-V power supply voltage has successfully switched a 1.2-Gbps signal. The power consumption of the LSI is 2.4 W. Pulsewidth variations occurring in the matrix switch circuit have been effectively reduced within ±80 ps by utilizing a compensation method employing cascaded gates. This GaAs 8×8 matrix switch LSI can be used for cross-connect systems, video switchers for TV studios and future broadband ISDNs, including HDTV services.

articleTitle: High Speed Dynamic Circuits Implemented with GaAs Mesfets
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The first reported dynamic domino (1) and "hot clock" (2) circuits using GaAs depletion-mode MESFETs are described. The domino AND gates were designed, fabricated and tested. The measured propagation delay per gate is 180ps for a 2-input AND gate and 220ps for a 4-input AND gate, respectively, with power consumption of 0.55mW/gate. A delay of 400ps is predicted for a 4-bit carry generator implemented by the domino circuit. A hot clock Johnson counter was designed and layed out. Simulations predict a very high operating frequency, 2GHz. These results show that dynamic GaAs FET circuits are promising for various high speed, low power applications.

articleTitle: An Ultra High Performance Manufacturaba GaAs E/D Process
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A recessed gate process suitable for manufacturing high performance GaAs enhancement/depletion mode digital integrated circuits is described. This process has been optimized to yield devices with performance equal to or better than self-aligned devices of similar geometry. The process is built around the heart of a proven depletion mode technology in order to insure its manufacturability. Using this process, we have successfully fabricated state-of-the-art E/D circuits with propagation delays as low as 44 pS and a speed power product of only 15 fJ. ECL compatible dividers were also fabricated and operated at clock rates of 2.9 GHz at a power dissipation of only 18 mM.

articleTitle: High Performance GaAs/AIGaAs Heterojunction Bipolar Transistor 4-Bit and 2-Bit A/D Converters and 8-Bit D/A Converter
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: GaAs/AIGaAs heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBT) have been used to develop high performance MSI-LSI circuits for analog-to-digital conversion (ADC) and digital-to-analog conversion (DAC) functions. A 4-bit parallel (flash) ADC with 850 transistors has an input bandwidth of >1.0 GHz at a clock rate of >1.0 gigasamples/second. The 4-bit ADC has on chip 15 current-mode logic (CML) master-slave comparators with preamplifiers, encoding logic for a binary output, and a reconstruction DAC output. To date this is the largest reported HBT CML circuit. The development of the 4-bit ADC was preceded by the design and evaluation of a 2-bit flash ADC (145 transistors) implementing similar on-chip functions. It has an input bandwidth of 1.25 GHz at a clock rate of 2.5 gigasamples/second. An 8-bit parallel DAC with 125 transistors is monotonie (without trimming) and has a DC RMS level error of 0.6 mV, less than a quarter of a least significant bit (LSB). The DAC settles to 8-bit accuracy in 1.7 ns. High speed functional circuit yield on the best wafer is >70% for the 2-bit ADC and >85% for the 8-bit DAC. The performance of these building block circuits demonstrates the potential for realizing 8-14 bit, 10 Ms/s to 3 Gs/s HBT A/D converter systems.

articleTitle: GaAs MMICs - Getting Those System Insertions
publicationTitle: 1987 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Practical considerations of GaAs MMIC technology insertions into existing and new sockets are discussed, and the distinctive characteristics of this technology are related to insertion opportunities.
